question: Following the Pahalgam attack in April 2025, India suspended which treaty with Pakistan?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indus Waters Treaty.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indus Waters Treaty:** The **Indus Waters Treaty** was signed in **1960** between **India** and **Pakistan**, with the mediation of the **World Bank**. It is a water-sharing treaty that governs the use of the Indus River system.
 
• This treaty allocates the use of six rivers in the Indus River system: **Indus, Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas**, and **Sutlej**.
 
• The treaty permits Pakistan to use the waters of the **Indus, Jhelum, and Chenab rivers** while granting India control over the waters of the **Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej** rivers.
 
• Despite multiple conflicts between the two nations, including the **1965 and 1971 wars**, the treaty has been upheld, making it one of the most successful water-sharing agreements in history.
 
• Following the **Pahalgam attack in April 2025**, India decided to suspend the treaty as a response to the escalating tensions between the two countries. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*
 
• The suspension of the treaty highlights the geopolitical tensions between India and Pakistan, as water resources are a critical issue for both nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tashkent Agreement:**

 
 
• The **Tashkent Agreement** was a peace agreement signed on **January 10, 1966**, between **India** and **Pakistan** after the **1965 Indo-Pak war**.
 
• It was mediated by the Soviet Union and signed in **Tashkent, Uzbekistan** (then part of the Soviet Union).
 
• The agreement aimed to restore economic and diplomatic relations between the two countries and withdraw their armed forces to pre-war positions.
 
 
 
• **Simla Agreement:**
 
 
• The **Simla Agreement** was signed on **July 2, 1972**, between **India** and **Pakistan** after the **1971 war** that led to the creation of Bangladesh.
 
• It aimed to establish lasting peace and outlined principles such as resolving disputes through peaceful means and mutual respect for sovereignty.
 
• This agreement also led to the conversion of the **ceasefire line in Jammu and Kashmir** into the **Line of Control (LoC)**.
 
 
 
• **Lahore Treaty:**
 
 
• Although there is no formal treaty named the Lahore Treaty, the **Lahore Declaration** was signed on **February 21, 1999**, between **India** and **Pakistan** to improve bilateral relations.
 
• It emphasized the need for both countries to avoid conflicts and nuclear arms race and to resolve disputes through peaceful dialogue.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact of Indus Waters Treaty Suspension:**

 
 
• The treaty's suspension could lead to significant water management challenges for **Pakistan**, as the Indus River system is a lifeline for its agriculture and economy.
 
• It could also escalate tensions between the two nuclear-armed neighbors, potentially impacting regional stability in **South Asia**.
 
• India's decision to suspend the treaty demonstrates its resolve to address cross-border terrorism and use water diplomacy as leverage.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Treaty:**
 
 
• The **Indus Waters Treaty** is vital for ensuring water security in the region and fostering cooperation between India and Pakistan.
 
• Its suspension highlights the interdependence of natural resources and geopolitics in international relations.
